Basis of approval, recorded precisely so a later reader can judge its weight: the word list below was transcribed into this file by an unattended agent session (issue #130, PR #250), which recorded the sourceUrl, retrievedAt and sha256 above as the exact bytes it read (185,852 bytes). Those values are PRESERVED here verbatim and are not re-asserted by this approval — see what was not done, below. What IS independently checkable today, with no network access at all, is this list's internal consistency and its fitness for its one consumer: expandVocabulary (prisma/content/english-vocabulary.ts) expands every "/" alternative and tokenises each through the full normalizeAnswer pipeline, and english-content-validator.spec.ts exercises that over this real file — every token of all 20 real writing sentences resolves against THIS list and not the reading one, and the two lists' genuine divergence is asserted directly in both directions ("taxes" is here and not on the reading list; "colors" is on the reading list and not here). What was NOT done, stated plainly rather than implied: no comparison against the official USCIS PDF was possible for this approval. uscis.gov returns HTTP 403 from the environment this work was done in and web.archive.org is unreachable, so the sha256 above was not re-derived from a freshly downloaded document and the byte count was not re-checked; there was no page-by-page human re-read of the rendered PDF either, then or now. What this status does NOT certify: that this list matches the official Writing Vocabulary list in content or in revision (rev. 08/08 is the revision the earlier session recorded, not one verified here); that no word is MISSING — an omission is invisible to every check above, because a missing word only ever shows up as a legitimate sentence failing validation, which no shipped sentence currently does; or that USCIS has published nothing newer since 2026-09-04. USCIS M-1178 (09/17) warns explicitly that the reading and writing lists overlap but ARE NOT THE SAME: "When creating your sentences, keep the lists and activities separate." Do not merge them — the validator enforces that separation and a merge would defeat it. A maintainer revising this file from a network-capable environment should re-download the source, re-hash it, diff the extracted text against this list, and rewrite this note to say what they actually did rather than inheriting this one.
